title: Status Page Signal Gap Audit (v0.6) — components lacking reliable signals + proposed indicators
content:
Context
- This doc is the working gap audit for “Status page transparency upgrades”. Goal: each public status component should have reliable, low-latency signals that (a) correctly represent customer impact and (b) can be used to auto-suggest components + impact language in incident comms.
- Target audience: SRE/oncall + Observability + component owners.
- Non-goal: define the customer-facing taxonomy itself (see Confluence taxonomy proposal). This doc is purely about signal coverage and “what we can measure confidently”.

Current problem statement (from incidents + Support)
- We often mark “API Degraded” because we lack a streaming-only or model-family-specific signal with enough confidence.
- Region ambiguity: internal alerts fire for a single serving cluster, but our customer-visible signals are global aggregates.
- Partial failure modes (stream disconnects, 429s on specific routes, rerank timeouts) don’t show up in the same top-level error rate graphs that oncall uses during incidents.

How we evaluated coverage
- For each public component, we looked for:
  1) A primary “impact” metric with clear customer correlation (errors/timeouts/availability).
  2) One latency metric (p50/p95/p99) scoped to the component.
  3) Minimum viable segmentation labels: region, route, model_family (where relevant), and customer_tier (optional).
  4) Alertability: low false positive rate at severity thresholds we can defend.
  5) Ability to backfill “what changed” during incident review (logs/traces/event annotations).
- Sources reviewed:
  - Datadog dashboards for gateway + serving + console (existing)
  - Prometheus metrics in hosted control plane services
  - Incident timelines from the last ~6 weeks (manual sampling) + the most common “status page confusion” Support tickets

Public components in scope (from taxonomy draft)
Hosted API
- API Gateway (requests, auth, 4xx/5xx, 429)
- Streaming (SSE/websocket-ish streaming response path)
- Text Generation (non-streamed completion)
- Embeddings
- Rerank
- Capacity & Routing (scheduler/routing, fallback behavior, capacity constraints)
- Hosted Serving (Region: us-east, us-west, eu-west) — may be represented as regional child components
Console
- Console UI + API
- Rollouts (model version pinning + deployment controls)
Enterprise
- Dedicated Control Plane
- Private Control Plane

Summary of findings (TL;DR)
- Strong coverage: API Gateway baseline error/latency, Hosted Serving GPU saturation (but needs better customer-facing mapping), Console basic uptime.
- Weak coverage (highest priority): Streaming disconnects/partial failures, route-level 429s vs real “outage”, model_family scoping, and “Capacity & Routing” signals that explain degraded performance without 5xx.
- Biggest structural gap: inconsistent tagging across services. We need “status_component” and a small set of standard labels on key metrics. This is the basis of slo-toolkit PR_88 + redwood PR_48244.

Gap table (by component)
Legend
- Coverage: Good / Partial / Weak
- Confidence: High / Medium / Low (how confidently we can reflect customer impact)
- Latency to detect: <2m / <10m / >10m

1) API Gateway
Coverage: Good | Confidence: High | Latency to detect: <2m
Existing signals
- gateway_request_total (by route, status_code)
- gateway_5xx_rate (global) + gateway_latency_p95 (global)
- auth_failures_total
Gaps
- Clear differentiation between customer-caused 4xx vs platform-caused (e.g., 429 due to capacity vs account quota)
- Region scoping is inconsistent (gateway is global edge; serving is regional)
Proposed additions
- gateway_429_rate labeled by reason={capacity, quota, rate_limit_policy, unknown}
- gateway_request_latency_p95 labeled by route_group (chat/embeddings/rerank/stream)
- Create “customer-impact” derived metric: gateway_platform_error_rate = 5xx + timeouts + 429(reason=capacity)
Owners
- Amara Diallo (gateway) + Aisha Bello (derived metric definition)

2) Streaming
Coverage: Weak | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <2m (if instrumented)
Existing signals
- streaming_disconnects_total exists but not consistently emitted across all serving paths; missing region + route labels
- gateway_200_rate masks streaming issues (customers get 200 then disconnect)
Observed failure modes (from recent incidents)
- Keepalive timeout causing mid-stream disconnects
- Upstream backpressure causing stalls (no tokens emitted for >N seconds)
Gaps
- No first-class metric for “stream started but did not complete normally”
- No metric for “time-to-first-token” vs “token cadence stalls”
Proposed additions
- stream_session_completed_total labeled outcome={success, client_disconnect, server_disconnect, upstream_timeout, internal_error}
- stream_time_to_first_token_ms histogram labeled region, model_family
- stream_token_cadence_seconds gauge or derived distribution: max gap between tokens over the session
- Add log-based indicator (temporary until metrics are stable): count of “stream closed: code=…” aggregated by region/model_family
Notes
- We should treat “server_disconnect spike” as Degraded Performance for Streaming component (not full API outage) unless accompanied by gateway platform error spike
Owners
- Ethan Park (serving instrumentation), Christine Wong (status mapping), Mina Haddad (region scoping)

3) Text Generation (non-streamed)
Coverage: Partial | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <10m
Existing signals
- serving_5xx_rate (global) + serving_latency_p95 (global) exists but aggregates streaming + non-streaming
Gaps
- Route separation is weak; non-stream requests should have independent latency/error
- Model_family scoping missing (we need to distinguish “mixtral family failing” vs all models)
Proposed additions
- request_success_total labeled route_group=text_generation and model_family
- request_latency_ms histogram labeled route_group, model_family, region
- Add “queue_wait_ms” histogram from scheduler/routing layer to distinguish capacity-driven latency
Owner
- Mina Haddad (route + region labels), Ethan Park (model_family label)

4) Embeddings
Coverage: Partial | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <10m
Existing signals
- embeddings_request_total and embeddings_latency_p95 exist but missing region label in ~40% of samples (observed)
- Error rate is captured but not broken down by failure mode (timeout vs input too large vs upstream)
Gaps
- Customer-visible impact often is “timeouts” rather than 5xx
- Need a clean “server timeout” and “deadline exceeded” counter
Proposed additions
- embeddings_errors_total labeled error_class={timeout, internal, bad_request, rate_limit, upstream}
- embeddings_deadline_exceeded_total
- embeddings_latency_ms histogram labeled region
- Add simple saturation indicator: embeddings_concurrency (in-flight) by region
Owners
- Ethan Park + Aisha Bello (definitions)

5) Rerank
Coverage: Weak | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: >10m currently
Existing signals
- rerank_request_total exists in app metrics but not in shared dashboard; error signal is sporadic
Gaps
- “Slow-but-successful” is the common incident pattern; we currently only see it via customer reports
- No dedicated rerank latency SLO chart
Proposed additions
- rerank_latency_ms histogram labeled region, model_family
- rerank_timeout_total labeled region
- rerank_upstream_error_total labeled provider={internal, external_dependency} (do not expose provider name in public comms)
- Alert: rerank_p95 > threshold for 10m + elevated timeouts
Owners
- Aisha Bello (dashboard + alert), Ethan Park (instrumentation)

6) Capacity & Routing
Coverage: Weak | Confidence: Low-to-Medium | Latency to detect: <10m (if implemented)
What this component needs to represent
- “Platform is up but constrained”: high queue times, increased 429(reason=capacity), fallback activation, elevated retries, capacity shortfall in a region
Existing signals
- GPU utilization and queue depth exist but not correlated/visible to oncall in a comms-friendly way
- Fallback events are not consistently emitted as metrics
Gaps
- No clean single indicator we can point to during incident updates (“customers may see increased 429s; mitigation: use fallback model/other region”)
Proposed additions
- routing_fallback_activated_total labeled from_model_family, to_model_family, reason={capacity, health, policy}
- scheduler_queue_wait_ms histogram labeled region, route_group
- capacity_shortfall_gauge labeled region (computed: demand - supply) OR at least “serving_admission_rejects_total” labeled region
- 429 capacity reason tagging in gateway (ties back to API Gateway proposed additions)
Owners
- Mina Haddad (routing), Amara Diallo (429 reason), Allison Grant (dashboard design)

7) Hosted Serving — Regional components (us-east / us-west / eu-west)
Coverage: Partial | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <10m
Existing signals
- Region-level serving health exists for some metrics; others are global aggregates
Gaps
- Inconsistent region label cardinality and naming (use us-east vs use1, etc.)
- Lack of “region pinned” traffic metrics (how many customers are pinned to impacted region)
Proposed additions
- Standard region label normalization (region={us-east, us-west, eu-west}) in instrumentation pipeline
- serving_platform_error_rate per region + route_group
- “pinned_traffic_share” estimate: percent of traffic with region=explicit vs auto (helpful for comms but optional)
Owners
- Mina Haddad + Allison Grant

8) Console (UI + API)
Coverage: Partial | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <10m
Existing signals
- Console uptime checks exist; basic 5xx metrics exist
Gaps
- Rollouts UX issues (stuck rollout, canary not progressing) show as “success” from a simple ping
- Need key flows instrumentation: login, model selection, rollout create/update
Proposed additions
- console_flow_success_total labeled flow={login, view_model, create_rollout, update_rollout}
- console_api_5xx_rate labeled endpoint_group
- Synthetic checks for rollout create/update (low frequency)
Owners
- Nora Ahmed (console), Marissa Cole (requirements)

9) Dedicated Control Plane
Coverage: Partial | Confidence: Medium | Latency to detect: <10m
Existing signals
- Control plane API uptime and error rate (not always tenant-scoped)
Gaps
- Need tenant isolation: a single Dedicated tenant issue shouldn’t always look like “Dedicated CP down”
- But we also need a public signal for control plane-wide degradation
Proposed additions
- dedicated_cp_platform_error_rate (aggregate) + dedicated_cp_tenant_error_rate (internal-only)
- Public component should key off platform_error_rate + multi-tenant symptom threshold
Disclosure note
- For external status, do NOT include tenant identifiers. Use internal dashboards to decide if it’s tenant-specific vs platform-wide.
Owners
- Dylan Brooks (tooling) + Rafael Mendes (SRE)

10) Private Control Plane
Coverage: Weak (for public status relevance) | Confidence: Low
Notes
- Private deployments are frequently customer-network-dependent; we should be careful not to publish misleading global signals.
Gaps
- We lack a reliable aggregate signal because private environments vary.
Proposed approach
- For status page: only mark “Private Control Plane” if Redwood-managed control plane services (e.g., licensing/updates) are impacted across multiple private customers or if a hosted dependency impacts all private control planes.
- Internally: track “private_cp_update_success_rate” (aggregated) + “license_validation_errors_total”.
Owners
- Christine Wong + Security/Compliance consulted for wording

Cross-cutting requirements (blocking gaps)
1) Standard labels
- region: normalized (us-east, us-west, eu-west)
- route_group: chat | text_generation | streaming | embeddings | rerank | console
- model_family: e.g., llama3, mixtral, qwen (exact list in serving catalog)
- status_component: one of the public components (or mapping-friendly internal enum)
Status
- slo-toolkit PR_88 adds “status_component” tagging support to incident/SLO events.
- redwood PR_48244 adds region+route labels to selected error metrics (streaming disconnects, 5xx).

2) Derived “customer impact classifier” helper
- Needed so oncall sees consistent language: “Degraded performance” vs “Partial outage” based on observable thresholds.
- Inputs should include:
  - gateway_platform_error_rate
  - component-specific error rate
  - component-specific latency regression
  - streaming server disconnect spike
  - queue_wait regression
- Output: suggested impact language + suggested components.
Tracking: Linear ENG-4828.

3) Alerting philosophy for status comms
- We should not page on every “status component degraded” signal; we should use these signals to *inform* comms once an incident exists, and to reduce time-to-clarity.
- However, some signals (streaming server disconnect spike, gateway platform errors) should be primary alert routes.

Proposed dashboards (mock notes / layout)
Dashboard: “Status Components — Impact Overview” (top-level)
- Row 1 (global):
  - API Gateway platform error rate (stacked: 5xx, timeouts, 429 capacity)
  - Streaming server_disconnect rate + time_to_first_token p95
  - Embeddings error rate (timeout vs other) + latency p95
  - Rerank latency p95 + timeouts
  - Console flow success rate (login + rollout create)
- Row 2 (regional breakdown):
  - Hosted Serving platform error rate by region (small multiples)
  - Queue wait p95 by region (small multiples)
  - Fallback activated total by region (bar/time series)
- Row 3 (triage aids):
  - Top routes by error contribution (route_group + endpoint_group)
  - Top model_families by error contribution
  - Recent deploy/event annotations overlay (from structured incident annotations / PR_48219)

Dashboard: “Incident Comms Evidence Pack” (per-incident quick link)
- A templated view with pre-filtered time range around incident start
- Includes: component health, change events, and a pre-filled “what’s impacted” checklist for oncall
- Note: we can generate this link from incident-bot once incident ID exists.

Data quality checks (must-have before we trust signals)
- Cardinality guardrails: model_family + region + route_group is OK; avoid model_id label unless sampled.
- Sampling: traces are fine sampled, but metrics must be complete for error counters.
- Region label completeness should be >99% on key metrics.

Prioritization (next 2 weeks)
P0 (blockers for status page accuracy)
- Streaming: session outcome + server disconnect reason; time-to-first-token
- Gateway: 429 reason tagging (capacity vs quota)
- Serving: route_group + region labels on error/latency
- Routing: queue_wait_ms + fallback_activated metrics
P1
- Embeddings: timeout classification + latency by region
- Rerank: p95 latency + timeouts
- Console: key flow success metrics
P2
- Dedicated/Private control plane refinements (public criteria + internal-only detail)

Open questions / risks
- What thresholds do we commit to for “Degraded” vs “Partial outage” per component? (Needs alignment with SRE severity + customer impact language)
- Streaming stall detection: do we standardize on “no token for >30s” vs “TTFT > X”? Need a few days of baseline data.
- Fallback metrics: ensure we don’t imply we always fallback successfully (comms templates need uncertainty language).
- Provider dependency labeling: we should track internally but not leak vendor-specific details externally.

Action items (owners + dates)
- [Ethan Park] Implement stream_session_completed_total + TTFT histogram (ETA 2024-07-12)
- [Amara Diallo] Add gateway 429 reason tagging (ETA 2024-07-10)
- [Mina Haddad] Normalize region labels for serving metrics + queue_wait histogram (ETA 2024-07-15)
- [Aisha Bello] Draft derived “platform error rate” queries + initial thresholds (ETA 2024-07-09)
- [Allison Grant] Publish first dashboard draft “Status Components — Impact Overview” (ETA 2024-07-16)
- [Christine Wong] Validate mapping of proposed metrics -> status components with oncall scenarios (ETA 2024-07-18)

Appendix: notes from recent incidents (sanitized)
- Incident A: Customers reported “streaming cuts out mid-response”. Gateway showed normal 200 rates; serving 5xx flat. Only clue was scattered logs “keepalive timeout”. This is the canonical case for streaming-outcome and TTFT/cadence.
- Incident B: Elevated 429s in us-west. Some were legitimate quota enforcement; others were capacity. Without tagging, oncall hesitated to declare component impact. Need 429 reason tagging + queue wait to support “Capacity & Routing degraded in us-west”.

Appendix: proposed metric naming conventions (draft)
- <component>_<signal>_<unit> e.g., streaming_time_to_first_token_ms
- Error counters should be <component>_errors_total with error_class
- Latency histograms should end with _ms and be standard buckets across components

Changelog
- v0.6 (2024-07-03): added Capacity & Routing proposed signals; clarified Dedicated/Private external criteria; updated linked artifacts for PR_48244 and PR_48219.
- v0.5 (2024-06-26): initial gap table + dashboard mock notes.
